Going around USD to EUR to GBP and back to USD (accent arrows) costs −0.10 − 0.15 + 0.20 = −0.05, a negative cycle: an arbitrage loop. The card returns the cycle with its first node repeated at the end, USD, EUR, GBP, USD." width="100%"} Returns one negative cycle that can be reached from `source`, as the list of nodes around it (the first node repeated at the end). Use it to locate the arbitrage loop or the modelling error behind a failed shortest-path computation (see `negative_edge_cycle()`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to search from, as an ID or label. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs around the cycle, with the first node repeated at the end. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source` does not exist or no negative cycle is reachable from it. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Bellman-Ford from `source`, keeping predecessors. A node still improving in round $V$ is reachable from a negative cycle; following predecessors $V$ times lands on the cycle, which is then read off by following predecessors until it closes. It runs in $O(VE)$ time. NetworkX's `find_negative_cycle` can fail with "Negative cycle is detected but not found" on some graphs where this method succeeds. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#c030b68a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec fx = ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True).add_nodes(["USD", "EUR", "GBP"]) fx.add_edges([("USD", "EUR", -0.10), ("EUR", "GBP", -0.15), ("GBP", "USD", 0.20)]) [fx.get_label_from_id(n) for n in fx.find_negative_cycle("USD")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['USD', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'USD'] ``` ::: :::
